mainTopic: The size, placement and tying of ציצית, and whether making a מצוה item needs a ברכה
overview: The גמרא first explains that ציצית, like לולב, have no maximum length but do have a minimum. A ברייתא then teaches that ציצית means hanging strands, and אביי adds that they must be partly loose. Next comes a מחלוקת about attaching the strings at the very tip of the corner or on the border. רב's rule that ציצית must hang down onto the corner follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. רבי יעקב requires the hole to be at least a thumb joint from the edge, and together with רב פפא's rule this sets a range. A story with רבינא shows that this distance only matters when the ציצית are made. The גמרא lists three ways of tying the strings, then asks whether tying ציצית needs a ברכה. This leads to רב חסדא's rule linking a גוי's ability to make a מצוה item with whether a Jew says a ברכה. The rule is tested on מילה and supported by סוכה, and the refutation from תפילין continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No maximum length, but there is a minimum
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'ציצית has no measure' means there is no upper limit, though there is a lower limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: ציצית have no maximum measure, but they do have a minimum measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what an earlier teaching meant when it said ציצית 'have no שיעור.' It means the strings can be as long as you like, but not too short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'no שיעור' could sound like any length works, even a tiny one. The גמרא narrows it: the missing limit is only the top limit. A bottom limit still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A set measurement or size requirement

steps.confusionAlert: 'No שיעור' here does NOT mean any length is fine. It only means there is no maximum.

phrases.english: It has no measure upward (no maximum),
phrases.notes: 'It' is ציצית. The גמרא is explaining an earlier teaching that said ציצית have no measure.

phrases.english: but it does have a measure downward (a minimum).

steps.triggerLanguage: אין לה שיעור למעלה אבל יש לה שיעור למטה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording of a teaching quoted just before this passage
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of a phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No שיעור' might mean there is no length requirement at all
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the maximum is missing; a minimum length still applies

steps.title: Comparing to לולב, which also has 'no measure'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a proof: לולב is also described as having no measure, yet surely it has some minimum.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, then in the similar case where a לולב is said to have no measure, would you say it has no measure at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof by comparing ציצית to לולב. It asks: would we really say a לולב has no size rule at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, 'no שיעור,' are used for לולב. If those words meant 'no limit at all,' then a tiny לולב would work too. The question expects the answer 'no,' and the next step shows why.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so
Similar to it, a parallel case
The palm branch taken on סוכות

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,

phrases.aramaic: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ לוּלָב אֵין לוֹ שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: in a similar case, 'a lulav has no measure,'

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאֵין לוֹ שִׁיעוּר כְּלָל?
phrases.english: would it also mean it has no measure at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: דאי לא תימא הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins proving the explanation given in step 1
steps.raayaObject: That 'no שיעור' means only no maximum
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel wording used for לולב

steps.title: The משנה shows לולב needs three טפחים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a לולב of three טפחים is valid, proving it has a minimum size.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: a לולב that is three טפחים long, enough to wave with it, is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that sets a minimum length for a לולב. This proves that 'no שיעור' cannot mean there is no limit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a לולב needs three טפחים so it can be shaken, then a shorter one is not valid. So לולב has a minimum even though it is called 'without measure.' The same wording for ציצית can be read the same way.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: לוּלָב שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: A lulav that has three handbreadths
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in סוכה, דף כט עמוד ב.

phrases.english: enough to wave with it, is fit,

steps.triggerLanguage: והתנן לולב שיש בו שלשה טפחים כדי לנענע בו כשר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that answers the rhetorical question of step 2
steps.raayaObject: That לולב has a minimum size despite having 'no measure'
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in סוכה requiring three טפחים

steps.title: Both לולב and ציצית have a minimum but no maximum
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that לולב has no maximum but has a minimum, and the same is true of ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a לולב has no maximum measure but does have a minimum measure. So too, ציצית have no maximum measure but do have a minimum measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. Just as לולב has a minimum but no maximum, ציצית also have a minimum but no maximum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forced us to read 'no שיעור' for לולב as 'no maximum.' Since the same words are used for ציצית, they mean the same thing there. This confirms the explanation from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, the same applies here

steps.whatToRemember: When ציצית or לולב are said to have 'no שיעור,' it means no maximum. Both still have a minimum size.

phrases.english: Rather: it has no measure upward,
but it has a measure downward;

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי אֵין לוֹ שִׁיעוּר לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: so too, it has no measure upward,
phrases.notes: Now 'it' means ציצית: the same rule carries over from לולב.

phrases.english: but it has a measure downward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אין לו שיעור למעלה אבל יש לו שיעור למטה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the לולב proof and applies it to ציצית
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ציצית have a minimum length but no maximum, just like לולב

steps.title: The word ציצית means hanging strands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ציצית means hanging strands, proven from a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'ציצת' means nothing but hanging strands, as it says: 'And he took me by a lock of my head.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא explains that the word ציצית in the תורה means strands that hang down, and brings a פסוק where the same word means a lock of hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's word ציצת is defined by comparing it to יחזקאל, where ציצת ראשי means a lock of hair. A lock of hair hangs loose. So ציצית must also be loose, hanging strands.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (introduces a supporting פסוק)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'Tzitzit' –
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:38

phrases.english: tzitzit means nothing but hanging strands,
and so it says:
'And he took me by a lock of my head,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 8:3

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן ציצת אין ציצית אלא ענף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: what ציצית are made to look like
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית must be hanging strands, as shown from the meaning of the word in יחזקאל

steps.title: אביי: the strings must be partly loose
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the strings must be separated and hang loose, like a gentile's lock of hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: One must separate the strings like the lock of hair of non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a practical detail to the ברייתא. The strings must be left loose and separated, like a certain style of hair lock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said ציצית are hanging strands. אביי explains what that looks like in practice: part of the strings is bound and the rest hangs loose and separated, like a lock of hair that is braided and then left loose.
steps.whatToRemember: ציצית must have hanging, separated strands, not be fully wound up.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: And one must separate it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ציצית, meaning the hanging strings.

phrases.english: like the lock of hair of gentiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמר אביי וצריך לפרודה כי צוציתא דארמאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical application to the definition in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציצית strings must be separated and hang loose

steps.title: Strings attached at the corner tip or the border are valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that ציצית attached at the very tip of the corner or on the edge-border are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If one attached the strings at the tip of the corner, or on the border, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא begins about where on the garment the strings may be attached. The first opinion says even the very tip of the corner or the edge-border works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how close to the edge the ציצית may be placed. This first opinion is lenient and accepts both the corner tip and the edge-border. The next step brings a disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: Corner, here the very tip of the corner
The woven border along the garment's edge

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If one attached it to the tip of the corner,
or to the border – it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן הטיל על הקרן או על הגדיל כשירה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: where on the garment the strings may be placed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית attached at the corner tip or on the border are valid

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב invalidates both
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees and says ציצית in either spot are invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב invalidates them in both cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with the first opinion. In his view, strings at the corner tip or on the border are both invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a מחלוקת. The תנא קמא allows both placements, while רבי אליעזר בן יעקב requires the strings to be placed further in from the edge than either of these spots.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת: the תנא קמא allows strings at the corner tip or on the border; רבי אליעזר בן יעקב invalidates both.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov (says)
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: disqualifies in both of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב אומר פוסל בשתיהן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dissenting opinion against the ruling in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית placed at the corner tip or on the border are invalid

steps.title: Whose view does רב's ruling follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא agrees with רב's rule that ציצית must hang down onto the corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what רב גידל said in the name of רב: ציצית must hang down onto the corner, as the פסוק says, 'on the corners of their garments'? Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ruling of רב and asks which side of the argument we just saw it fits with. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says the strings must hang down onto the corner. That means the hole is made above the corner, not at its very tip or on its border. Since the תנאים just argued about exactly this point, the גמרא wants to know which side רב is following.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom does this go? A question asking which earlier opinion a ruling follows
Literally 'dripping'; here it means hanging down
The corners of their garments (from the פסוק of ציצית)

phrases.english: According to whom does this go,
what Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: צִיצִית צְרִיכָה שֶׁתְּהֵא נוֹטֶפֶת עַל הַקֶּרֶן,
phrases.english: Tzitzis must hang down onto the corner,
as it is said: 'On the corners of their garments,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:38

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects an אמורא's ruling to the מחלוקת תנאים in steps 7–8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does רב's rule that ציצית must hang onto the corner follow?

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב's ruling matches רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who disqualified ציצית placed at the tip or on the border.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב agrees with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said ציצית at the very tip of the corner or on the border are not valid. If they must be placed above the corner, they will naturally hang down onto it, which is what רב requires. The תנא קמא of the same ברייתא, who allowed the tip and the border, would not require this.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב, an אמורא, rules like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב against the תנא קמא. That matters for the practical placement of the hole.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who requires the ציצית to be above the corner and not at its tip or border.

steps.title: The hole must be a full thumb joint from the edge
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב, in the name of רבי יוחנן, rules that the hole must be at least a thumb joint away from the edge of the garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: And one must keep the hole a full thumb joint away from the edge.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is brought about the minimum distance between the ציצית hole and the edge of the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a minimum: the hole cannot be closer to the edge than a thumb joint. It fits with the idea that ציצית should not be right at the border.

keyTerms.meaning: He must distance, meaning keep the hole away from the edge
A thumb joint, the length from the tip of the thumb to its first joint

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
And one must distance
phrases.notes: He means the hole for the strings, measured from the edge of the garment.

phrases.english: a full thumb joint.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a measured minimum distance for the hole's placement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציצית hole must be at least a full thumb joint away from the edge of the garment.

steps.title: Why רבי יעקב's rule is needed alongside רב פפא's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that with only רב פפא's 'within three fingerbreadths' rule, we might think closer is always better, so רבי יעקב's minimum was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both רב פפא's statement and רבי יעקב's statement were needed. If we had only רב פפא's, I would have thought 'within three' means only not farther than that, and the closer the better. So רבי יעקב's statement was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why we need two separate rules about where the hole goes. This is the first half, and the second half comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא set a maximum: the hole must be within three fingerbreadths of the edge. On its own, that could suggest the closest spot is ideal. רבי יעקב's rule adds a minimum, so the hole cannot be right at the edge.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed, showing that a statement teaches something new
I would have said, the mistaken assumption we might have made
Within three fingerbreadths, רב פפא's maximum distance

steps.confusionAlert: Neither rule argues with the other. רב פפא gives the farthest the hole may be, and רבי יעקב gives the closest. Together they set a range.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa's statement was needed,
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא's rule from the previous daf: the hole must be within three fingerbreadths of the edge.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Ya'akov's statement was needed,
for if we had only Rav Pappa's, I would have said:
'within three' means only not to distance it more,
and the closer it is, the better;
so Rabbi Ya'akov's statement was needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ דְּרַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Justifies the need for step 11's rule given רב פפא's earlier rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without רבי יעקב, one might think the hole is best placed as close to the edge as possible.

steps.title: Why רב פפא's rule is needed alongside רבי יעקב's
steps.stepSummary: With only רבי יעקב's minimum, we might think farther is always better, so רב פפא's maximum was needed. Therefore both rules are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only רבי יעקב's statement, I would have thought 'a full thumb joint' means only not closer than that, and the farther the better. So both were needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation and concludes that both rules are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב's minimum alone might suggest placing the hole far up the garment. רב פפא's 'within three fingerbreadths' caps the distance. The result is that the hole goes between a thumb joint and three fingerbreadths from the edge.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed. The conclusion that each statement teaches something the other does not

steps.whatToRemember: The ציצית hole must be at least a thumb joint (רבי יעקב) and no more than three fingerbreadths (רב פפא) from the edge, and the ציצית hang down onto the corner, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.english: And if we had only Rabbi Ya'akov's, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: מְלֹא קֶשֶׁר גּוּדָל, דְּלָא לִיקְרַב טְפֵי,
phrases.english: 'a full thumb joint' means only not to bring it closer,
and the farther it is, the better;
therefore both were needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי מִדְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided explanation begun in step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rules are necessary: together they place the hole between a thumb joint and three fingerbreadths from the edge.

steps.title: רב סמא questions רבינא's torn cloak
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא notices that the corner of רבינא's cloak tore, so the hole is now less than a thumb joint from the edge. He challenges רבינא: don't you follow רבי יעקב's rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא and רב סמא were sitting before רב אשי. רב סמא saw that the corner of רבינא's cloak had torn, so the hole was now less than a full thumb joint from the edge. He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold of רבי יעקב's rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that tests the rule from Step 11. רב סמא thinks רבינא's ציצית are now invalid because the hole is too close to the edge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב said the hole must be at least a thumb joint from the edge. Here the cloth tore after the ציצית were tied, so the hole ended up too close. רב סמא assumes the rule must be kept at every moment, not just when the ציצית are made.

keyTerms.meaning: Thumb joint, the minimum distance from the edge

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא וְרַב סַמָּא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Ravina and Rav Samma were sitting before Rav Ashi.
Rav Samma saw
the corner of Ravina's cloak
that had torn, and was less than a full thumb joint.
phrases.notes: Because the cloth ripped, the hole was now closer to the edge than a thumb joint.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold
of that rule of Rabbi Ya'akov?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יעקב's minimum-distance rule to a real case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's practice of wearing the cloak with the torn corner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the hole must be at least a thumb joint from the edge, a hole that ends up closer should make the ציצית invalid.

steps.title: The rule applies only when the ציצית are made
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that רבי יעקב's minimum distance was said for the time the ציצית are made. A later tear doesn't make them invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was said for the time of making.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends himself. The thumb-joint distance only has to be right when the ציצית are first tied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows רבי יעקב's rule: it is about how the ציצית are made, not something that must stay true forever. Since רבינא's hole was far enough away when he tied the strings, the later tear doesn't matter.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of making (the ציצית)

steps.whatToRemember: The thumb-joint minimum is checked when the ציצית are made. If the garment tears later and the hole ends up closer to the edge, the ציצית stay valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule: a ציצית garment that tears near the hole after the strings were tied does not need to be redone.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was stated for the time of making.
phrases.notes: In other words, the distance only has to be right when you tie the ציצית on.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּיה אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב סמא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule to the time of making
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thumb-joint distance must stay in place the whole time the garment is worn.
steps.terutzMaskana: The distance is only required when the ציצית are first made.

steps.title: רב אשי comforts the embarrassed רב סמא
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא is embarrassed by his mistake. רב אשי tells him not to be upset, because one of them is like two of us.
steps.simpleTranslation: He became embarrassed. רב אשי said to him: Don't be upset; one of them is like two of us.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב אשי encouraging רב סמא after his mistaken question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. רב אשי softens the moment by telling רב סמא there is no shame in being corrected by a scholar of such high stature.

phrases.english: He became embarrassed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא תִּתְּקִיף לָךְ,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him: Do not be upset.
One of them is like two of us.
phrases.notes: 'Them' and 'us' are two groups of scholars. A common reading is the scholars of ארץ ישראל compared with those of בבל.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּתְּקִיף לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after רבינא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not a legal ruling; רב אשי encourages רב סמא after his error.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב's method of folding and looping
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב placed four strings, folded them, put them through the hole, and looped them. He held that there must be eight strands in the garment, to fulfill "גדיל גדילים" when making the hanging strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב would place four strings, fold them over, insert them into the cloak, and loop them through. He held that we need eight in the garment, so that there is "גדיל" "גדילים" at the place of the hanging string.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how the strings are attached to the garment. First it describes רב אחא בר יעקב's method and his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Folding four strings in half and pushing the folds through the hole gives eight strands on one side and four loops on the other. He then pulls the strands through the loops. His reason is that the פסוק's word "גדילים" calls for doubled strands right where the hanging strings are formed.

keyTerms.meaning: Twisted cord, twisted cords (from the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the numbers: he starts with four strings, but after folding them there are eight strands in the garment.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב רָמֵי אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: Rav Aha bar Ya'akov would place four strings,
and fold them over,
and insert them into the cloak,
and loop them through.
He holds: we need eight in the cloak,
so that there will be "twisted cord," "twisted cords"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:12

phrases.english: at the place of the hanging string.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב רָמֵי אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the hole's distance to how the strings are attached.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four strings are folded, inserted, and looped, so that there are eight strands in the garment, because of "גדיל גדילים".

steps.title: רב ירמיה מדפתי uses eight strings without looping
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדפתי placed eight strings, which became sixteen hanging ends, and did not loop them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה מדפתי would place eight strings, which are sixteen, and he did not loop them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second method of attaching ציצית, different from רב אחא בר יעקב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of folding and looping, he puts eight strings through the hole, so both ends hang down and give sixteen. He doubles the number of strings and leaves out the looping step.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti would place eight,
which are sixteen,
phrases.notes: Each string goes through the hole with both ends hanging down, so eight strings give sixteen ends.

phrases.english: and he did not loop them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִרְמְיָה מִדִּפְתִּי רָמֵי תְּמָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different method from רב אחא בר יעקב's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight strings are placed through the hole (sixteen ends) without looping.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא does it like us
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא attached ציצית the way we do: four strings through the hole, making eight ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא would do it like ours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the list of methods with the one that matches common practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Like ours" means four strings put through the hole with both ends hanging, giving eight, with no folding-and-looping and no doubling to sixteen. This is the simplest of the three methods.

keyTerms.meaning: Like ours, the way we do it

steps.whatToRemember: Three methods of attaching ציצית: רב אחא בר יעקב folded and looped four strings into eight strands, רב ירמיה מדפתי used eight strings (sixteen ends) without looping, and מר בריה דרבינא used four strings making eight ends, like our practice.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, would do it like ours.
phrases.notes: 'Like ours' means four strings through the hole with both ends hanging down, making eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא עָבֵיד כְּדִידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third method, the familiar one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four strings are inserted so that eight ends hang down, without looping.

steps.title: רב נחמן stops a ברכה on tying ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן sees רב אדא בר אהבה say a ברכה while tying ציצית. He quotes רב that ציצית need no ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן found רב אדא בר אהבה putting strings on a garment and saying the ברכה 'to make ציצית.' He said to him: 'What is this "tzitzi" sound I hear? רב said that ציצית do not need a ברכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: A story: רב נחמן objects to a ברכה said while tying ציצית. He quotes רב's ruling that no ברכה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not about wearing ציצית. It is about the act of tying them onto the garment. According to רב, the tying itself gets no ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'to make ציצית', the ברכה said over tying them

steps.confusionAlert: This is about the ברכה on tying ציצית, not the ברכה on wearing them.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: Rav Nachman found Rav Adda bar Ahava
putting strings onto a garment
and saying the blessing "to make tzitzit."
He said to him: What is this "tzitzi" that I am hearing?
phrases.notes: He is poking fun at the sound of the ברכה, as if to say 'what's all this tzitzi-tzitzi?' The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: This is what Rav said:
Tzitzit do not require a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה רָמֵי חוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: after the ways of tying ציצית, the גמרא turns to whether tying needs a ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, tying ציצית does not require a ברכה.

steps.title: רב חסדא contrasts two teachings of רב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks how רב could say no ברכה is needed. רב also taught that ציצית made by a גוי are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא died, רב חסדא went into the study hall to point out a contradiction between two teachings of רב. Did רב really say ציצית need no ברכה? But רב יהודה said in רב's name: how do we know ציצית made by a גוי are פסול? The פסוק says 'Speak to the children of Israel and they shall make ציצית.' Jews shall make them, and not גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges רב's ruling about the ברכה. He sets it against another ruling of רב, that a גוי's ציצית are invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we only hear the two statements. We do not yet hear why they clash. One says no ברכה on tying. The other says only a Jew may tie ציצית. The next step asks what the actual contradiction is.

keyTerms.meaning: he passed away (literally, his soul rested)
to set one teaching of רב against another of רב

phrases.english: When Rav Huna passed away,

phrases.aramaic: עָל רַב חִסְדָּא לְמִירְמֵא דְּרַב אַדְּרַב,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda went in to raise a contradiction between Rav and Rav:
And did Rav really say:
Tzitzit do not need a blessing?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that tzitzit made by a non-Jew are invalid?
As it says: "Speak to the children of Israel
and they shall make for themselves tzitzit"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:38

phrases.english: The children of Israel shall make them,
and the non-Jews shall not make them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב: צִיצִית אֵין צָרִיךְ בְּרָכָה? וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רב quoted by רב נחמן in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that tying ציצית needs no ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself taught that a גוי's ציצית are פסול. That seems to make the tying a real מצוה act, which should get a ברכה.

steps.title: What is the contradiction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why these two teachings of רב clash at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what is the contradiction?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the problem is. One teaching is about a ברכה and the other is about who may make ציצית. This sets up רב יוסף's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface the two rulings deal with different things. So the גמרא needs an extra idea that links 'who may do it' with 'whether a ברכה is said.'

phrases.english: But what is the contradiction?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מַאי רוּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of רב חסדא's challenge in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What link between the two rulings of רב makes them contradict each other?

steps.title: רב יוסף explains רב חסדא's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רב חסדא held a rule. If a מצוה is valid when a גוי does it, a Jew says no ברכה. If it is invalid when a גוי does it, a Jew must say a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב חסדא holds that any מצוה valid when done by a גוי needs no ברכה when a Jew does it. Any מצוה invalid when done by a גוי needs a ברכה when a Jew does it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question of step 22. He gives the rule that links 'can a גוי do it' to 'does a Jew say a ברכה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this rule, the contradiction is clear. רב said a גוי's ציצית are פסול, so tying ציצית should need a ברכה. Yet רב also said it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds / is of the opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the engine of the next part of the סוגיא. The גמרא will now test whether it really holds.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: קָסָבַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Rav Chisda holds:
Any מצוה that is valid when done by a non-Jew,
when a Jew does it, he does not need to say a blessing.
Any מצוה that is invalid when done by a non-Jew,
when a Jew does it, he needs to say a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: קָסָבַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא assumed that a מצוה a גוי cannot validly do needs a ברכה when a Jew does it. So רב's ruling that a גוי's ציצית are פסול clashes with his ruling of no ברכה.

steps.title: Is that really a rule? The case of circumcision
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב חסדא's rule using מילה, which a גוי may perform. It brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about which non-Jewish doctor is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this a fixed rule? What about מילה, which is valid when done by a גוי? A ברייתא teaches: a city with no Jewish doctor, but with an Aramean doctor and a כותי doctor, the Aramean should circumcise and not the כותי, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the כותי, and not the Aramean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to attack רב חסדא's rule. It brings proof that a גוי may perform מילה. The full point of the attack continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, both opinions let a non-Jew circumcise. They only argue about which one. So מילה is כשירה when a גוי does it. By רב חסדא's rule, a Jew should then say no ברכה on it, and the גמרא is about to point out the problem with that.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה do not argue about whether a non-Jew may circumcise. Both allow it. They only argue about which non-Jew is better.

phrases.english: And is this a fixed rule?
But there is circumcision, which is valid when done by a non-Jew,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: עִיר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ רוֹפֵא יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא: A city that has no Jewish doctor,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בָּהּ רוֹפֵא אַרְמַאי וְרוֹפֵא כּוּתִי
phrases.english: but has an Aramean doctor and a Samaritan doctor,
the Aramean should circumcise and the Samaritan should not circumcise;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כּוּתִי וְלֹא אַרְמַאי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: The Samaritan, and not the Aramean.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְלָלָא הוּא? וַהֲרֵי מִילָה דִּכְשֵׁירָה בְּגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule that רב יוסף attributed to רב חסדא in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a מצוה valid by a גוי needs no ברכה when done by a Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מילה is valid when done by a גוי, as the ברייתא shows. Yet the גמרא is about to show that a Jew does say a ברכה on מילה, which breaks the rule.

steps.title: Yet a Jew doing מילה must say a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is completed. מילה is valid when done by a גוי, but a Jew who does מילה still says a ברכה, which goes against רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when a Jew does it, he must say a ברכה. The Master taught: the one who does the מילה says, 'Blessed... Who made us holy with His מצוות and commanded us about מילה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it began in step 24. Even though a גוי may do מילה, a Jew who does it must say a ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule said that if a מצוה is valid when a גוי does it, a Jew says no ברכה. מילה breaks this rule: a גוי may do it, yet a Jew says a ברכה. So the rule looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who does the מילה
And commanded us about מילה (the words of the ברכה)

phrases.english: And when a Jew does it, he must recite a blessing,
as the Master said: The one who circumcises says:
"Blessed... Who has sanctified us with His מצוות
and has commanded us concerning circumcision."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a מצוה valid when done by a גוי needs no ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מילה is valid when done by a גוי, yet a Jew who does it says a ברכה. That is the opposite of what the rule predicts.

steps.title: The rule only needs to fit רב, who holds that מילה by a גוי is פסול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא's rule was made to explain רב. According to רב, מילה done by a גוי is פסול, so מילה fits the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this matter for anyone except רב? And רב holds that מילה done by a גוי is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב חסדא's rule was only made to explain רב's opinions, and רב says a גוי's מילה is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי's מילה is פסול, the rule says a Jew must make a ברכה, and that is exactly what happens. So for רב, מילה supports the rule instead of breaking it. The ברייתא in step 24, which lets a גוי do מילה, simply does not follow רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there any reason (to need this) except for... — the rule only has to fit one person
He fully disqualifies it (holds it is פסול)

phrases.english: Is there reason to explain this according to anyone but Rav?
Rav invalidates it,
phrases.notes: He means מילה done by a גוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי הוּא טַעְמָא, אֶלָּא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 24-25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to one אמורא's view: רב holds that a גוי's מילה is פסול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the rule had to fit every opinion, including the ברייתא that allows a גוי to do מילה
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only has to fit רב. For רב, a גוי's מילה is פסול, so a Jew's ברכה matches the rule

steps.title: Proof that רב invalidates מילה by a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב really holds this. דרו בר פפא quotes רב, who learns it from the פסוק 'And you shall keep My covenant.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was said: From where do we know that מילה by a גוי is not valid? דרו בר פפא said in the name of רב: 'And you shall keep My covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that רב really said a גוי's מילה is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to אברהם and his children: 'you shall keep My covenant.' רב learns from it that only those who belong to the covenant may do מילה. This backs up the answer in step 26.

phrases.english: As it was stated: From where do we know
that circumcision by a gentile is not valid?

phrases.aramaic: דָּרוּ בַּר פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר:
phrases.english: Daru bar Pappa said in the name of Rav:
"And as for you, you shall keep My covenant."
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:9

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: מִנַּיִן לְמִילָה בְּגוֹי שֶׁפְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 26 about רב's view
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds a גוי's מילה is פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: דרו בר פפא quoting רב, based on 'ואתה את בריתי תשמר'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: only a circumcised person may do מילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן agrees that a גוי's מילה is פסול, but he learns it from a different פסוק: 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל', read as 'the circumcised one shall circumcise.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל' — the one who is circumcised shall circumcise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source for the same law. This one comes from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק repeats the verb 'מול'. רבי יוחנן reads the extra word to teach that only someone who is himself circumcised (הַמָּל) may do מילה for others. רב uses the 'covenant' idea, while רבי יוחנן uses the 'circumcised person' idea.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall surely be circumcised (a doubled verb in the פסוק)
The one who is circumcised shall circumcise

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
"He must surely be circumcised,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 17:13

phrases.english: the one who is circumcised shall circumcise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הִמּוֹל יִמּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the same law as step 27
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה must be done by someone who is circumcised, so a גוי's מילה is פסול

steps.title: The law of סוכה supports רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the law of סוכה supports רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: סוכה supports him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests רב חסדא's rule against other מצוות. It says that the law of סוכה fits the rule and supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule connects two things: whether a גוי may make the item, and whether a Jew says a ברכה when making it. The גמרא says סוכה fits this pattern. It will spell out the details afterward.

phrases.english: Sukka supports him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב חסדא and his rule about when a ברכה is said.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּכָּה מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מילה to testing the rule on other מצוות
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule linking a גוי's ability to make the item with whether a ברכה is said

steps.title: The law of תפילין refutes רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The law of תפילין is a strong refutation of רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפילין is a refutation of him.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the support from סוכה, the גמרא says that the law of תפילין goes against רב חסדא's rule. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא is a strong refutation, not just a question. סוכה fits the rule, but תפילין does not. So the rule cannot be fully correct, and the גמרא will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין worn on the head and arm

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא linked two questions: whether a גוי may make the item, and whether a Jew says a ברכה when making it. מילה fits this for רב, סוכה supports it, and תפילין refutes it.

phrases.english: Phylacteries are a refutation of him.
phrases.notes: This is a strong word: the law of תפילין knocks down רב חסדא's rule. The גמרא explains how next.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּפִילִּין הָוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 29: סוכה supports the rule, but תפילין refutes it
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule about when a ברכה is said
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The law of תפילין does not match what the rule predicts, so it counts as a strong refutation.

steps.title: A סוכה built by a גוי is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a ברייתא that a סוכה made by a גוי is כשר. This is the first half of showing that סוכה fits רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at סוכה: it is valid even when a גוי made it. A ברייתא teaches that a סוכה of גוים, of women, for animals, of כותים, or any סוכה at all is כשר, as long as it has proper סכך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining its earlier claim that סוכה supports רב חסדא. It starts by proving that a סוכה built by a גוי is כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule says that if a מצוה is כשר when a גוי makes it, a Jew who makes it does not say a ברכה on the making. So the first fact to prove is that a גוי's סוכה is כשר. The ברייתא shows that who built the סוכה does not matter at all, only the סכך does.

keyTerms.meaning: Covered with סכך the way the הלכה requires

phrases.english: Here is a sukka, which is valid when made by a gentile,
as it is taught in a baraita:
A booth of gentiles, a booth of women,
a booth for animals, a booth of Samaritans,
a booth of any sort is valid,
provided that it is roofed according to its halakha.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי סוּכָּה דִּכְשֵׁירָה בְּגוֹי, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 29's claim that סוכה supports רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule: a מצוה that is כשר when done by a גוי needs no ברכה on its making
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing that סוכות built by גוים, women, for animals, or by כותים are all כשר

steps.title: No ברכה is said on building a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that a Jew building a סוכה says שהחיינו and later לישב בסוכה, but never 'לעשות סוכה'. This completes the proof that סוכה fits רב חסדא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a Jew who builds a סוכה does not need to say a ברכה on building it. A ברייתא teaches: someone who builds a סוכה for himself says שהחיינו. When he comes to sit in it, he says 'אשר קדשנו במצוותיו וצונו לישב בסוכה'. But he does not say a ברכה of 'לעשות סוכה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes proving that סוכה supports רב חסדא. It shows that a Jew who builds a סוכה does not say a מצוה-ברכה on the building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the ברכות connected to a סוכה: שהחיינו at the building, and לישב בסוכה when sitting in it. Since 'לעשות סוכה' is missing from the list, there is no ברכה on the act of building. Together with step 31, this fits רב חסדא exactly: the מצוה is כשר by a גוי, so there is no ברכה on making it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה thanking הקב"ה for bringing us to this time
'To dwell in the סוכה', the ברכה said when sitting in it
'To make a סוכה', a ברכה on building, which is not said
He does not say a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: שהחיינו is said at the building, so it can look like there is a ברכה on making the סוכה. But שהחיינו is about reaching the יום טוב season. It is not a ברכה on the מצוה of building. The missing ברכה is 'לעשות סוכה'.
steps.whatToRemember: סוכה fits רב חסדא's rule perfectly: it is כשר when a גוי builds it, and a Jew says no 'לעשות סוכה' ברכה when building it.

phrases.english: And when made by a Jew, he does not need to recite a blessing,
as it is taught: One who makes a sukka for himself says:
"Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe,
Who has given us life, sustained us, and brought us to this time."
When he comes to sit in it, he says:
"Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ לֵישֵׁב בַּסּוּכָּה״,
phrases.english: Who has sanctified us with His מצוות and commanded us to sit in the sukka."
Whereas "to make a sukka" he does not bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 31 by showing the second half of רב חסדא's rule, that there is no ברכה on making it.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's rule, the no-ברכה side
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the ברכות on a סוכה (שהחיינו and לישב בסוכה) with no 'לעשות סוכה'

steps.title: תפילין refute the rule because they are invalid when made by a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts explaining why תפילין refute רב חסדא: תפילין made by a גוי are פסול, and it begins quoting רב חיננא בריה דרבא's ברייתא as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפילין are a refutation of רב חסדא. For תפילין are פסול when a גוי makes them, as רב חיננא the son of רבא taught...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its claim that תפילין refute רב חסדא and starts to explain why. First it sets up the fact that תפילין made by a גוי are פסול, and it begins quoting a source that the next lines will finish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, a מצוה that is פסול when a גוי does it should need a ברכה when a Jew does it. So the גמרא first proves that תפילין are פסול by a גוי. The rest of the refutation, that there is still no ברכה on making תפילין, comes in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid when made by a non-Jew

steps.whyThisMatters: A תיובתא is the strongest kind of attack in the גמרא. If the second half holds up, רב חסדא's rule cannot stand as a general rule.

phrases.english: Tefillin are a refutation of him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רב חסדא. The גמרא is now explaining the short claim it made just before.

phrases.english: for tefillin are invalid when made by a gentile,
as Rav Ḥinnana, son of Rava, taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּפִילִּין תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ, וַהֲרֵי תְּפִילִּין דִּפְסוּלוֹת בְּגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the סוכה support (steps 31-32), the גמרא goes back to step 30's claim about תפילין and begins to explain it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a מצוה which is פסול when a גוי does it requires a ברכה on its making
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין are פסול by a גוי, so by the rule a Jew making them should say a ברכה. The coming lines will show that he does not, which breaks the rule.
